questions.concept: Removing the condition from a conditional bound
questions.question: If an algorithm's behavior is bounded by "o(f(n)) if g(n)", what notation does it become when the condition is removed?
questions.explanation: A conditional bound o(f(n)) if g(n) states the bound o(f(n)) under condition g(n); dropping the condition (when f is smooth/well-behaved) leaves the unconditional bound o(f(n)). The condition g(n) is not part of the growth function.

questions.question: Contention-based MAC protocols are commonly used in:
questions.explanation: Ethernet uses CSMA/CD, a contention-based (random access) MAC protocol where stations compete for the medium. Token Ring uses controlled access with a token, so there is no contention.

questions.question:
Ginni has created a table, SCORES in MySQL to store runs scored by players in a cricket match. The table contains the following records:
Table: Scores
PLAYER | SCORE
Ranveer | 50
Sukesh | 35
Mirza | 10
John | 51
Murugan | 70
Which of the following statements will give 10 as output?
questions.explanation: The smallest score is 10 (Mirza), so MIN(Score) returns 10. MAX gives 70, SUM gives 216 and AVG gives 43.2.

questions.question: 1 Byte =?
questions.explanation: One byte consists of 8 bits; 4 bits is a nibble.

questions.question: Divide and Conquer is an algorithmic paradigm that solves problems by:
questions.explanation: Divide and conquer splits a problem into smaller subproblems, solves them recursively and combines their results. Greedy combination and heuristics belong to other paradigms.

questions.question: Math.h is a
questions.explanation: math.h is a C standard library header file that declares mathematical functions such as sqrt() and pow().

questions.question: The dual of a Boolean expression is obtained by

options.B: interchanging all 0s and 1s, all + and '.' signs
options.C: interchanging all 0s and 1s, all + and '.' signs and complementing all the variables
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: The dual is obtained by interchanging + with . and 0 with 1, leaving variables unchanged. Complementing the variables as well gives the complement of the expression, not the dual.

questions.question: In Audio and Video Compression, voice is sampled at 8000 samples per second with_____________
questions.explanation: Telephone-quality voice is sampled at 8000 samples/s with 8 bits per sample, giving 64 kbps. The other bit depths are not the standard.

questions.question: If NFA of 5 states excluding the initial state is converted into DFA, maximum possible number of states for the DFA is?
questions.explanation: The NFA has 5 + 1 = 6 states, so subset construction can produce at most 2^6 = 64 DFA states. 32 = 2^5 forgets the initial state.

questions.question: ZigBee architecture has ________ layers.
questions.explanation: The ZigBee stack has 5 layers: Physical and MAC (from IEEE 802.15.4), Network, Application Support sublayer and Application layer. 4 omits the application support sublayer.

questions.question: Which of the following provides the ability to query information from the database and insert tuples into, delete tuples from, and modify tuples in the database?
questions.explanation: Data Manipulation Language covers querying and inserting, deleting and modifying tuples. DDL defines the schema.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used for sending emails?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send email. HTTPS is for secure web access, FTP for file transfer and TCP is a transport protocol.

questions.question: Machine language is

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Machine language is written in binary for a specific processor, so it is machine dependent, difficult to program and error prone. All of A, B and C are true, hence 'More than one of the above'.

questions.concept: Default access in struct vs class
questions.question: How do structures and classes in C++ differ?

options.A: Structures by default hide every member whereas classes do not
options.B: In structures, members are public by default, whereas, in classes, they are private by default
options.C: Structures cannot have private members, whereas classes can have
options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: In C++ struct members are public by default while class members are private by default; otherwise they are equivalent and structs can have private members.

questions.question: ________ is the set of rules that governs how data can be transmitted over the World Wide Web.
questions.explanation: HTTP (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol) is the set of rules governing how data is transferred over the World Wide Web. Encryption standards and digital certificates are security mechanisms, not the transfer rules themselves.

questions.question: To which of the following the term "DBA" referred?
questions.explanation: DBA stands for Database Administrator, the person responsible for managing and maintaining a database system. 'Data Bank Administrator' is not the standard term.

questions.question: Which data structure is required to convert the infix to prefix notation?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Infix to prefix (or postfix) conversion uses a stack to hold operators and handle precedence.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a memory management technique used by operating systems?

options.D: More than one of the above

questions.explanation: Paging and segmentation are memory management techniques. Fragmentation is a problem (wasted memory) that memory management tries to reduce, not a technique.

questions.question: Which of the following operators evaluates to True if the variables on either side of the operator point to the same memory location and False otherwise?
questions.explanation: The identity operator 'is' returns True when both operands refer to the same object in memory. 'is not' returns the opposite.

questions.question: Which type of register is primarily used to temporarily hold data during arithmetic and logical operations in a microprocessor?
questions.explanation: The accumulator holds an operand and the result of arithmetic and logical operations in the ALU. Shift and counter registers have specialised purposes.

questions.question: Data transmission using multiple pathways simultaneously is known as:
questions.explanation: Parallel transmission sends several bits simultaneously over multiple lines. Serial uses one line, and duplex/half-duplex describe direction, not number of paths.

questions.question: Which metric is used for estimating the size of a software project?
questions.explanation: Function Points estimate software size from inputs, outputs, inquiries, files and interfaces. Cyclomatic complexity measures control-flow complexity and defect density measures quality.

questions.question: What is the key advantage of using a carry-lookahead adder instead of a ripple-carry adder?
questions.explanation: A carry-lookahead adder computes carries in parallel from generate and propagate signals, so it has much lower propagation delay than a ripple-carry adder. It actually uses more gates, is more complex and consumes more power.

questions.question: The class of CFG is not closed under:
questions.explanation: Context-free languages are closed under union, concatenation and Kleene star (repeated concatenation) but not under intersection, e.g. {a^n b^n c^m} intersected with {a^m b^n c^n} gives {a^n b^n c^n}, which is not context-free.

questions.question: Which among the following is/are true as per the ZigBee standards?
questions.explanation: ZigBee (IEEE 802.15.4 based) is designed for low-power, low-data-rate (up to 250 kbps), short-range wireless sensor networks, so all three statements are true.
